summary.headline: Sell narrowly scoped automation and cyber-readiness services before investing in software.
summary.best_opportunity: Productized cyber-hygiene and evidence-pack service for UK micro and small businesses.
summary.why_now: The 2025 UK government Cyber Security Breaches Survey says 43% of businesses identified a breach or attack in the prior 12 months—about 612,000 businesses—while small firms often lack dedicated security capacity. This is a live need signal, not proof of willingness to buy this specific offer.

top_opportunities.name: SME cyber-hygiene setup and monthly check-ins
top_opportunities.description: Fixed-scope baseline review, MFA and backup checks, staff phishing checklist, incident contacts and an evidence pack; refer technical remediation to qualified partners where needed.
top_opportunities.why_now: GOV.UK's 2025 survey reports 43% of businesses experienced an identified breach or attack in the previous year. The prevalence remains material despite falling from 50% in 2024.
top_opportunities.buyer: Small professional-services firms, charities and local businesses without in-house security staff.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £100–£600 using existing equipment and established tools; exclude formal certification and specialist insurance until validated.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Potentially 1–3 weeks through direct outreach and a paid baseline pilot; unverified estimate.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Medium-high: monthly checks, staff onboarding and evidence maintenance; retention must be tested.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: High for a software engineer comfortable with systems and automation; avoid claiming certification or penetration-testing expertise without qualifications.
risks: Liability and trust barriers; set a narrow scope and obtain appropriate professional advice/insurance.
Survey reports incidents, not buyer demand for this exact service; validate with paid pilots.
top_opportunities.verdict: Best initial test: low build cost and evidence-backed pain, but sell practical hygiene—not unsupported security guarantees.

top_opportunities.name: AI workflow automation for one local-service niche
top_opportunities.description: Implement lead triage, quote follow-up, appointment reminders and admin hand-offs using existing no-code/AI tools, with human review and documented fallback.
top_opportunities.why_now: AI interest is widely discussed, but this run did not obtain a reliable live UK adoption statistic. The opportunity is a hypothesis: buyers pay for measurable admin time saved, not AI branding.
top_opportunities.buyer: Small trades, clinics or agencies with repeated enquiries and missed follow-ups.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £100–£500 for a demo and initial tool subscriptions.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–3 weeks if sold as a paid workflow audit and fixed-scope implementation; estimate, validate locally.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Medium-high via monitoring, adjustments and support retainers.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Very high for a solo engineer who can integrate APIs and tailor workflows.
risks: Crowded provider market and uncertain willingness to pay without niche-specific ROI.
Privacy, data quality and automation failures require safeguards and human escalation.
top_opportunities.verdict: Strong runner-up; start service-led and only productize a repeated, paid workflow.

top_opportunities.name: Missed-enquiry recovery for trades and appointment businesses
top_opportunities.description: Set up web-form/phone lead capture, rapid acknowledgement and follow-up reminders, reporting booked appointments and response times.
top_opportunities.why_now: A direct revenue-linked service is easier to explain than generic software; current run found no robust live public data quantifying missed enquiries, so demand is a testable commercial hypothesis.
top_opportunities.buyer: Trades firms, repair services and appointment-based local businesses.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £100–£400 using existing CRM, messaging and automation services.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–2 weeks for a paid setup pilot; estimate dependent on outreach access.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: High potential through monthly monitoring and optimization.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: High; integrations and simple reporting are technically tractable.
risks: Existing CRMs may already solve the problem; demonstrate measurable incremental bookings.
Messaging consent, platform policies and personal-data handling must be checked.
top_opportunities.verdict: Fastest practical cash test if a reachable local niche and clear before/after metric are available.

top_opportunities.name: Website care and conversion improvements for local SMEs
top_opportunities.description: Monthly maintenance, backups, accessibility/basic performance checks and small conversion improvements for existing business websites.
top_opportunities.why_now: Recurring maintenance addresses ongoing operational work, but this run did not verify current UK market demand or competitor pricing; differentiate with a specific local-business segment and outcomes.
top_opportunities.buyer: Small firms relying on their website for enquiries but lacking in-house technical support.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £50–£300 with existing development tools and hosting arrangements.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–3 weeks via audits and a paid first-month package; estimate.
risks: Commodity competition and low willingness to pay for maintenance alone.
Scope creep and responsibility for third-party outages or compromised sites.
top_opportunities.verdict: Viable only when bundled with visible enquiry or reliability outcomes and strict scope.

top_opportunities.name: Vertical micro-SaaS for a manual compliance or admin task
top_opportunities.description: Build a tiny workflow tool for one underserved UK trade or professional niche after observing repeated manual work and securing paid design partners.
top_opportunities.why_now: A narrow workflow can support recurring revenue, but no validated niche, search demand or customer interviews were gathered in this run; demand evidence is weak until prospects pay.
top_opportunities.buyer: A specific trade association or small-firm segment with a repeated spreadsheet-based task.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £200–£1,500 for a lean prototype, excluding substantial marketing or legal advice.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Typically slower, 4–12+ weeks; highly uncertain without pre-sales.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: High potential if workflow is frequent and retention proven.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: High technically, but distribution and support are the main risks.
risks: Building before validating willingness to pay wastes time and budget.
Acquisition, compliance and ongoing support can exceed solo part-time capacity.
top_opportunities.verdict: Do not start with a build; interview and pre-sell a manual service first.

best_pick.name: SME cyber-hygiene setup and monthly check-ins
best_pick.why_it_wins: It combines a current UK government signal of substantial incident exposure with a low-capital, service-first route to revenue and a plausible monthly follow-on. Evidence supports the pain, not this offer's conversion rate; validate before investing.
validation_plan: Contact 15 small firms in one reachable sector; ask about recent security reviews, backups, MFA and who owns follow-up. Seek 3 discovery calls and at least 1 paid pilot.
Offer a fixed-scope baseline to 3 prospects; record objections, delivery hours and willingness to continue monthly. Stop or revise if no paid pilot follows credible outreach.
best_pick.first_offer: £250 fixed-price, one-week cyber-hygiene baseline: short interview, MFA/backup/access checklist, prioritized actions and evidence summary; explicitly not a certification, audit or penetration test.
best_pick.mvp: A secure checklist and reusable report template, with manual review and optional monthly action tracking; avoid collecting credentials or sensitive production data.
customer_types: Local charities and other small organizations without dedicated IT/security staff
best_pick.do_today: Draft a one-page scope and exclusions, then send 10 personalized outreach messages to one sector and request a paid pilot conversation.
